title: The drive-analytics README still describes InternalTransmitterUpdate strands, an interface the reactor replaced with onOperations before v6.2.2-dev.74
content:
`packages/common/drive-analytics/README.md` states that the processor "implements the `IProcessor` interface and processes `InternalTransmitterUpdate` strands, which contain sequences of operations performed on document drives."

At v6.2.2-dev.74 that interface no longer exists. `packages/shared/processors/types.ts:54` declares `onOperations(operations: OperationWithContext[]): Promise<void>`, and a search of the tree finds **no `onStrands` and no `InternalTransmitterUpdate`** in package sources. This is the same drift the relational-DB processor spec shows, from the same v6 processor migration.

What the README gets right and is worth trusting: the two processors, the `DriveOperations` counter, all four dimension path formats, the five action-type verbs, chunked processing with a default of 50, and the clear-and-rebuild-from-index-0 behaviour. None of those depend on the delivery interface.

So the reading rule for this file: **the dimensional model is current, the delivery API is not.** A developer copying its architecture section into a new processor will write a method the reactor never calls — a failure that is silent, because a processor with no matching method simply receives nothing.
